```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, fig.width = 6.5, fig.height = 0.3)

# draws n full-width blank lines (margin to margin) for handwritten answers,
# as a single plot so spacing is deterministic; pair with fig.height = 0.3 * n
blank_lines <- function(n = 1) {
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0))
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, n), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "")
  for (i in seq_len(n)) {
    segments(0, n - i + 0.5, 1, n - i + 0.5, lwd = 1)
  }
}

# fill-in table drawn with base graphics so row height is controllable;
# body = list of rows, each a list/vector of cell strings ("" = blank)
blank_table <- function(headers, body, col_widths = NULL,
                        header_height = 0.35, row_height = 0.5, cex = 0.95) {
  nc <- length(headers); nr <- length(body)
  if (is.null(col_widths)) col_widths <- rep(1, nc)
  col_widths <- col_widths / sum(col_widths)
  cx <- c(0, cumsum(col_widths))
  h_total <- header_height + nr * row_height
  par(mar = c(0, 0, 0, 0), family = "serif")
  plot(NA, xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, h_total), axes = FALSE, xlab = "", ylab = "",
       xaxs = "i", yaxs = "i")
  y <- h_total
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  y <- y - header_height
  segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = 1.5)
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    y <- y - row_height
    segments(0, y, 1, y, lwd = if (i == nr) 1.5 else 0.5,
             col = if (i == nr) "black" else "grey70")
  }
  for (v in cx) segments(v, 0, v, h_total, lwd = 1)
  for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
    text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, h_total - header_height / 2, headers[[j]], font = 2, cex = cex)
  }
  y <- h_total - header_height
  for (i in seq_len(nr)) {
    for (j in seq_len(nc)) {
      if (!identical(body[[i]][[j]], "")) {
        text((cx[j] + cx[j + 1]) / 2, y - row_height / 2, body[[i]][[j]], cex = cex)
      }
    }
    y <- y - row_height
  }
}
```

**NRES 746, Week 11, Lecture 1: Linear or Not?**

Name: ___________________________________________

**Instructions:** Work alone on Part 1 (about 5 minutes), then compare
with a neighbor for Part 2. Keep laptops closed.

## Part 1: Sort the models (individual)

Here are six models for a response $Y$ and a continuous predictor $x$.
In (f), $a_{\text{site}}$ means a separate intercept for each of three
sites.

(a) $Y \sim \text{Normal}(a + bx + cx^2,\ \sigma^2)$

(b) $Y \sim \text{Normal}(a x^b,\ \sigma^2)$

(c) $Y \sim \text{Normal}(a + b \log x,\ \sigma^2)$

(d) $Y \sim \text{Poisson}(e^{a + bx})$

(e) $Y \sim \text{Normal}\left(\dfrac{ax}{b + x},\ \sigma^2\right)$

(f) $Y \sim \text{Normal}(a_{\text{site}} + bx,\ \sigma^2)$

**1a.** For each model, is the mean a linear function of the parameters
(yes/no)? Could `lm()` fit it as written? Could `glm()`?

```{r sort-table, fig.height=0.35 + 6 * 0.45}
blank_table(c("Model", "Linear in the parameters?", "lm()?", "glm()?"),
            lapply(c("(a)", "(b)", "(c)", "(d)", "(e)", "(f)"), function(m) c(m, "", "", "")),
            col_widths = c(0.8, 2.2, 1.2, 1.2), row_height = 0.45)
```

## Part 2: Compare (with a neighbor)

**2a.** Taking logs of the mean in (b) gives
$\log(ax^b) = \log a + b\log x$, which is linear. Does that mean
`lm(log(y) ~ log(x))` fits model (b)? What would it assume about the
noise?

```{r fig.height=0.3*4}
blank_lines(4)
```
